name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 263 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 37% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 263 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 37 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: In Manipur Kuki volunteers were shot dead and five Kuki men were found mutilated, sparking protests in Kangpokpi and Noney with police using tear gas and batons. In Kashmir a terror financing probe linked to LeT led authorities to search four locations, while an Indian national was killed in an attack on a commercial vessel near Oman. A Tata Sumo crash in Ramban killed one person and injured two. A Supreme Court bail petition was filed by Yumlembam Jiban Singh, accused of parading Kuki women naked, citing trial delays. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: I Manipur ble Kuki-frivillige skutt og fem Kuki-menn ble funnet lemlestet, noe som utløste protester i Kangpokpi og Noney med politi som brukte tåregass og batonger. I Kashmir førte en etterforskning av terrorfinansiering knyttet til LeT til at myndighetene søkte fire lokasjoner, mens en indisk nasjonal ble drept i et angrep på et handelsskip nær Oman. En Tata-Sumo-ulykke i Ramban drepte én person og såret to. En søknad om løslatelse fra Høyesterett ble innlevert av Yumlembam Jiban Singh, anklaget for å ha partert Kuki-kvinner nakne, med henvisning til forsinkelser i rettssaken. 437 dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
